candidates.title: ESR x Craig & Karl’s “Pocket Full of Joy” accessories give your iPhone more personality than your wallpaper
candidates.full_text:
My phone spends a shocking amount of its life face down on a desk, which means the side I actually look at most is the case. ESR seems to have done the same math. The accessory maker has teamed up with Craig & Karl, the art duo known for bold color, chunky graphics, and characters with very cheerful faces, on a collection called Pocket Full of Joy. It includes MagSafe cases for the iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro, their Pro Max siblings, and Apple’s new foldable iPhone Duo, plus matching magnetic wallets (compatible with the non-foldable models).

Craig Redman lives in New York and Karl Maier lives in London, and the two Brisbane-born artists have been making work together across that time difference since 2011. Their stuff tends to show up big, on bridges in Brisbane, a mini-golf course in London’s Canary Wharf, and gallery walls, including a current show at Cairns Art Gallery. Here, they’ve shrunk their graphics to fit in your hand. One case is a sticker-bombed collage, another features a giant polka-dot K, and the wallets literally say “HI.” Prices start at $29.99 for the wallets and $45.99 for the cases.

Designers: Craig Redman & Karl Maier for ESR

The collage case looks like someone emptied a sticker sheet onto the back of your phone, and I mean that as a compliment. A pink polka-dot heart sits at the center with a hand clutching a phone inside it, surrounded by a rainbow, a palm tree, stars, a “CRAIG & KARL” banner, and an ESR logo in yellow and red. Every element gets the duo’s signature thick black outline, which keeps the pile looking crisp instead of messy. The trick is the spacing: each sticker gets a little breathing room. The Pro versions float everything on a light backdrop, while the iPhone Duo version puts the same arrangement on black, making the pinks and yellows stand out.

Underneath the art sits ESR’s Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case with Camera Control and Flex Stand, sized for the iPhone 17 Pro, 18 Pro, and both Pro Max models. Flip out the Flex Stand and your phone props itself up anywhere from 15 to 69 degrees, ready for a FaceTime catch-up, a recipe video, or a lazy Sunday episode in bed. ESR claims 1,500g of magnetic hold, so your wallet or MagSafe charger snaps on and stays put while you dash out the door. Clumsy mornings are covered too, with ESR rating the case for 16-foot (4.9m) drops and raised lips guarding the screen and cameras. A built-in Camera Control cover keeps Apple’s camera button ready for spontaneous snaps, and both sizes cost $45.99, while the iPhone Duo starts at $49.99

Click Here to Buy Now: $45.99 | Amazon Link Here.

The second design goes bigger and simpler, with a giant polka-dot letter K in sunny yellow anchoring the bottom half of the case and a little smile tucked into its middle. Perched on top is a red, rocket-shaped character with two dot eyes, standing in front of a bright blue circle and holding a tiny phone that is also grinning. Giving letters faces is a classic Craig & Karl move, and here it turns a single letter into a mascot for your phone. The large graphic should be easy to spot on a crowded café table. It comes on the Pro and Pro Max cases too, but on the black iPhone Duo version, all that yellow practically glows.

Both designs also fit Apple’s foldable iPhone Duo, and here the Flex Stand gets a fun upgrade: it rotates a full 180 degrees. Fold the Duo shut for a quick video call, or open it to the 7.6-inch inner screen for a movie on the train, and the stand props it up either way, so the entertainment keeps rolling. Flip the same loop around and it becomes a finger grip, letting you take the fun wherever you go, from your morning commute to Sunday brunch. ESR claims 1,500g of magnetic hold for wallets and chargers, and full hinge coverage and raised edges keep the foldable protected. The Duo case costs $49.99, while the Pro and Pro Max versions cost $45.99.

Every wallet greets you with a chunky polka-dot HI and a little yellow character peeking out from the I. It’s a cheerful thing to see every time you pull out a card, and honestly a nicer hello than most people give before their morning coffee. The two blue wallets put red dots on the letters, while the black Grip version switches to blue dots and adds a bright red finger loop down the middle. The company rates their magnetic holding force at 2,000g, rising to 3,200g when paired with its magnetic cases. candidates.title: GADGETEER Daily Wrap: an OLED that handles a bright room, a Dutch oven in Cerise and three Seiko automatics on one movement
candidates.full_text:
Monday ran from a 55-inch OLED to a red Dutch oven, with a power station, a self-washing robot vacuum, a blacked-out folder and three automatic watches in between. Black Friday pricing did the heavy lifting all day, across televisions, kitchen gear, power gear and watches alike. The deepest cut took 43 percent off a robot vacuum that washes its own mops and dries them with warm air at its dock.

LG rates the C5 panel’s black at or below 0.24 nit in rooms lit up to 500 lux, a figure UL verified rather than a brochure guess. Movie nights keep their shadows in that kind of light, and Sunday football keeps its contrast in the same room on a bright afternoon.

The 55-inch set runs 120Hz native with VRR up to 144Hz and four full-speed HDMI 2.1 ports. Amazon has it at $949.95, down $300 from $1,249.95. Bright room or dark, it holds.

The full LG C5 piece walks the panel ratings, the gaming ports and the prior-year C4 sitting above it on price.

LG C5 55 inch OLED evo AI 4K TV (OLED55C5PUA) 120Hz native, VRR up to 144Hz · alpha 9 AI Processor Gen8 · 4 x HDMI 2.1 Price: $949.95 $1,249.95 (save $300.00, 24% off) Where to buy: Buy on Amazon

Anker’s SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 holds 1,024Wh and puts out 2,000W through ten ports, with a 3,000W peak for the surge when a motor kicks on and a 10ms UPS switch for gear that hates a dropout. Five AC outlets carry the big loads, though two 140W USB-C ports charge a large laptop at full speed at the same time.

The whole station weighs 24.9 pounds, so it moves from garage shelf to campsite in one hand without a second trip for cables. Amazon’s Black Friday price is $529.99 against a $799 list, and that price covers the fastest recharging 1kWh station Anker sells today. One box, ten ports.

Our full Anker piece covers the recharge speed and the port layout. It also links our hands-on review of the station, with runtime notes and port by port results from our own test routine for anyone who wants the deep version first.

Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 Portable Power Station 1,024Wh LiFePO4 · 2,000W output, 3,000W peak · 10 ports · 10ms UPS switch · 24.9 pounds Price: $529.99 $799 (save $269.01, 34% off) Where to buy: Buy on Amazon

Roborock’s Qrevo S Pro sends the dirty work to its dock, which washes the dual spinning mops at 167°F, dries them with warm air and empties the dust bin on its own. Suction is rated at 18,500Pa, and the brushes underneath are built to shed pet hair instead of wearing it. An all-rubber main brush floats over uneven boards, and the side brush pushes hair toward the bristle ends instead of wrapping it around the hub.

Only the Black finish carries the $399.99 price, a $300 cut from the $699.99 list. The dock does the chores.

The full Roborock piece prices the White finish against it and covers the kitchen-floor test, where cereal, grit and tracked-in dirt collect along the baseboards.

Roborock Qrevo S Pro Robot Vacuum and Mop 18,500Pa suction · Dual spinning mops · Dock washes the pads at 167°F, dries them with warm air and empties its own dust bin · Black finish Price: $399.99 $699.99 (save $300, 43% off) Where to buy: Buy on Amazon

Le Creuset has cast these pots in France since 1925, and the 5.5-quart Signature Round Dutch Oven is still the piece the whole company hangs on, rated for five to six servings and oven safe to 500°F. Sear on the stove, slide the pot into the oven, then carry the whole thing straight to the table for serving, since enameled cast iron holds heat in a way thin steel never will.

A loaf of no-knead bread fits with headroom to rise, and a whole chicken browns across the wide base without crowding the pan. Amazon sells the Cerise finish at $311.88 today, against $454.95 at Le Creuset’s own store. It serves at the table.

The full Le Creuset piece covers the century of cast iron behind the shape. It also sizes the 5.5-quart pot against the smaller and larger rounds for cooks picking a first one for a household of four or five.

candidates.title: The SUPRA 42 Is a Memento Mori Watch for People Who Hate Wasting Time
candidates.full_text:
I check my watch maybe 80 times a day, and it has never once asked me what I’m doing with my life. Most watches are polite like that. They tell you it’s 3:47, you sigh about the meeting, and everyone moves on. The memento mori watches of the 17th century were far more audacious, often shaped like silver skulls with the dial hidden behind a hinged jaw. Every time their owners checked the hour, they also got a tiny lecture on mortality, which is a lot to ask of a Tuesday.

The SUPRA 42 from Dubai newcomer Cook & Re brings back some of that audacity, with a water-resistance rating of 656 feet (200m). Its power reserve gauge, named Memento Mori, sits at 6 o’clock in blood-red hazard stripes and drains as the Swiss Sellita movement winds down. Founder Endre Szakacs, who spent more than two decades in international banking before switching to watches, puts it bluntly: “The countdown started the day you were born.” The debut run is a First Edition of 50 numbered pieces in a colorway called Falcon Black. Cheery stuff, and I kind of love it.

Skull watches became fashionable in 17th-century Geneva, where Calvinist rules frowned on crosses and showy ornament but had no problem with a good reminder of death. Watchmakers obliged with silver cases shaped like craniums, many of which flipped open at the jaw to reveal an engraved dial inside. Jean Rousseau, a Geneva watchmaker and grandfather of philosopher Jean-Jacques Rousseau, signed movements for some of them. These were luxury objects carried by the wealthy, which makes them a delightfully mixed message. You paid a small fortune to be reminded that none of it follows you anywhere.

The Worshipful Company of Clockmakers in London owns a skull watch long nicknamed the “Mary Queen of Scots” watch, a name that has always outrun the evidence. Its leather travel case dates to somewhere between 1780 and 1850, roughly two centuries after the queen lost her head. The idea resurfaced in plastic in 2013, when Swedish inventor Fredrik Colting took the Tikker to Kickstarter. You filled out a life expectancy questionnaire, and the watch counted down your estimated remaining years, days, and seconds on an LCD screen. Backers pledging $39 apiece helped push it past its $25,000 goal, and the press promptly nicknamed it the death watch.

Inside the SUPRA 42 sits the Sellita SW270-1, a Swiss automatic built on the architecture of Sellita’s workhorse SW200-1, with a power reserve indicator added at 6 o’clock. That gauge tracks the energy left in the mainspring, the coiled strip of metal that powers the watch. The movement runs at 4Hz, with a rated power reserve of roughly 41 hours. Cook & Re dresses the indicator in red and white hazard stripes, tips the hour hand in matching red, and calls it Memento Mori, which is about as subtle as a skull with a hinged jaw.

A silver skull is pure symbolism, and Colting’s countdown was an actuarial guess dressed up as fate. The SUPRA 42 shows its own remaining running time, and if you leave it on the nightstand for two days, it stops. Keeping it running means wearing it or winding it, a fairly literal reading of the brand’s “Challenge Over Comfort” motto. The dial carries topographic contour lines, framed by a unidirectional compass bezel.

The case measures 42mm (about 1.65 inches) in 316L stainless steel, with a guarded crown, lumed sword hands, and an interchangeable strap offered in the brand’s red and white stripes. Szakacs conceived it in Dubai and had it made in Switzerland, despite starting with “no watchmaking background” and “no connections in Switzerland.” His obsession goes back to childhood, when he slept with a wristwatch on his pillow just to hear it tick. Losing his father prompted him to think about how little time any of us get. The 50 First Edition owners will be called Conquerors, which is a pretty strong opening line for any watch meetup.

Cook & Re is also taking a swipe at watch-industry waitlist games. “If something is genuinely rare, it doesn’t need games around its scarcity,” Szakacs says, adding that once the 50 pieces are gone, they’re gone. Allocation requests opened on November 1 at cookandre.com, and the brand hasn’t published pricing or shipping regions yet.
